description:
The image is taken from a high vantage point, looking out over a body of water with land in the distance. The perspective is slightly to the right of due south, providing a view of the Strait of Gibraltar and the coast of North Africa (Morocco) in the far distance, which is somewhat hazy.

In the foreground, to the right, a dark green coin-operated telescope is prominently visible, positioned behind a black metal railing. Below the telescope and railing, the hillside is covered in lush green Mediterranean vegetation, including trees and bushes, with some light-colored rocks and dry grass visible among them.

Midground features include the sparkling blue-grey water of the strait, dotted with numerous large ships, some appearing to be cargo vessels or tankers, at anchor or navigating. Along the immediate coastline below the viewpoint, some white buildings and structures are visible, nestled among the greenery.

The background consists of the distant landmass, which appears mountainous and extends across the horizon. The sky above is a clear, bright blue with very few clouds. The sun appears to be high in the sky, casting bright light on the scene.

highlights.text: In 711 AD, the Berber commander Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed these narrow straits with an invasion force of thousands, launching the Umayyad conquest of Hispania.
Upon landing, Tariq's army established a secure beachhead at the base of the Rock, which was subsequently named Jabal Tariq (Mount Tariq), eventually evolving into the name Gibraltar.
Before centuries of heavy military fortification transformed its appearance, the Rock's southern end was a wild, uninhabited Mediterranean scrubland.
